slides.text: It weighs every tray and pours only the feed that is missing.
slides.sub: Five trays, five scales and one moving hopper, set from the touch screen or a phone.

slides.text: Most poultry farms still feed and water their flock by hand.
slides.sub: It tires workers, takes time, and unmeasured feed means uneven portions for the hens.
slides.notes: Agriculture is the main livelihood of millions of Filipino families (PSA, 2023, as cited in Razonales et al., 2025). Chicken is the most common poultry because of its nutritional value and low cost (Eda et al., 2023). Feeding and watering practices affect its quality (Franco et al., 2020, as cited in Zhou et al., 2022). Most farms still do this manually, which leads to fatigue and inconsistent feed and water.

slides.title: A layer farm in San Pablo City, Laguna
slides.text: Laying hens are raised here for eggs. Workers check supplies, pour feed and look at the water several times a day.
slides.notes: The farm is in Barangay Del Remedio, San Pablo City. Layers need a nutrient-rich, consistent diet to sustain egg production.

slides.title: What manual feeding leaves behind

points.d: Feed is estimated by eye, not weighed, so trays get different amounts.
Nobody is told when the feed or water runs low.
Visual checks leave no data on how much feed was given or eaten.

slides.notes: Without weight-based feed measurement and timely notifications about low supply, consistent feeding and prompt response are hard. Without automated data collection, there are no accurate records to review.

slides.text: Reduce manual labor, minimize feed wastage and improve monitoring of feed and water.
slides.sub: For poultry farm owners in San Pablo City, through an automated system built on the Arduino Mega 2560 and the ESP32.
slides.notes: The general objective is to help poultry farm owners in San Pablo City, Laguna, improve their daily operations by designing and developing HyFePoul, which aims to reduce manual labor, minimize feed wastage, and provide better monitoring of feed and water availability.

slides.kicker: Specific objective 1 · Functions a to d
slides.title: Feeding, moving and measuring

items.label: a
items.d: Up to three times a day, set on the panel or the app, kept through power loss.

items.label: b
items.d: A chain carries the hopper along five trays between two limit switches, then home.

items.label: c
items.d: A 1 kg load cell under each tray stops the pour at its target.

items.label: d
items.d: An ultrasonic sensor warns, alerts the app and blocks a cycle when the hopper is nearly empty.

slides.notes:
a. Implementing programmable feeding schedules of up to three daily feeding times, with an adjustable feed dispensing amount, set through the Nextion display or the mobile application and retained during power interruptions.
b. Distributing feed through a chain-driven moving hopper that travels along five feeding trays, using home and end limit switches to determine its starting and ending positions, prevent movement beyond its limits, and return home after each cycle.
c. Dispensing user-defined quantities into each tray using a 1 kg load cell under each tray with HX711 amplifiers, stopping once the tray's target weight is reached.
d. Monitoring the hopper feed level with an ultrasonic sensor, notifying the app and sounding the buzzer at the low threshold, and preventing or stopping a cycle when the hopper is nearly empty.

slides.kicker: Specific objective 1 · Functions e to g
slides.title: Water, screen and app

items.label: e
items.d: A float switch in the gravity-fed reservoir sounds the buzzer and alerts the app.

items.label: f
items.d: A 7-inch Nextion screen shows status, weights and schedules, and starts a feed.

items.label: g
items.d: Sign in, link the device, monitor, set schedules, feed and get alerts.

slides.notes:
e. Monitoring the water level in the gravity-fed reservoir using a float switch, notifying the app and activating the buzzer when manual replenishment is needed.
f. Providing a Nextion display that shows operational status, tray feed weights, hopper level, water status and schedules, allows an on-demand feed, and presents recent records.
g. Developing a mobile application for signing in, linking the device, viewing status and history, opening the Google Sheets log, adjusting schedules, starting a manual feed, and receiving notifications.

slides.kicker: Specific objective 1 · Functions h to j
slides.title: Records, connection and power

items.label: h
items.d: Data goes to Firebase and is copied to a Google Sheet, one tab per month.

items.label: i
items.d: The ESP32 sends timely updates. Offline, the device keeps feeding and sends pending data later.

items.label: j
items.d: A 12 V battery keeps feeding, monitoring and safety running during outages.

slides.notes:
h. Recording tray weights, hopper level, water status and alerts in Firebase Realtime Database, copied periodically to Google Sheets with a new sheet each month. Schedules, calibration and daily totals are also kept on the controller.
i. Transmitting system data through the ESP32 over Wi-Fi, so the app receives timely updates, while the device keeps its schedules and safety functions offline and sends pending alerts and records once connected.
j. Providing a battery backup that powers all components during main power interruptions, except internet-dependent functions.

slides.title: How farms feed and water today

points.d: Manual feeding is still the norm on smallholder farms (Deni et al., 2026; Simon and Palaoag, 2024).
Birds drink about 1.5 to 2 times as much as they eat (El-Sabrout et al.).
Feed needs change with age and production stage (De Grano et al., 2025).
Continuous, automated monitoring of production (Zaharieva and Dunchev, 2025; Bist et al., 2026).
Arduino and ESP32 feeders close the cost gap in the Philippines (Araneta, 2025).
Closed, measured feeding replaces open troughs that waste feed.

slides.text: None of the reviewed systems weighs each tray and pours only what is missing.
slides.sub: Most estimate feed from motor run time or watch only the storage level. HyFePoul adds per-tray scales, water alerts and offline operation.
slides.notes: Load-cell studies (Asri, Anand, David and Galina, Hermawan) shaped the weighing. Scheduling studies (Mansur, Ajayi, Chaurasia, Lumban Tobing and Kusuma) led to the RTC and worm gear motor. Hydration studies (Karun, Tagacay, Hidzir and Ismail, Preethi) led to the float switch. Connectivity studies (Velasco, Laksono, Tagacay) led to the ESP32 and app.
